newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to award corn import quotas end March - CNPR.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to award corn import quotas end March - CNPR.

text.p: Mexico is set to award corn import quotas again toward the end of March, newspaper Reforma reported Wednesday.

Citing Abel Castellanos, head of National Confederation fo Rural Landowners (CNPR), Reforma said Mexico will need to import around three million tonnes of corn in 1997, down two million tonnes from the five million tonnes imported in 1996.

Annually, Mexico's Agriculture and Trade Ministries award import quotas to cover the corn deficit in the country and analyze when stocks in the country are at levels where imports are necessary to guarantee supplies.

Castellanos said the import quotas awarded will be lower this year because of the improved outlook for the national corn crop. He said the crop this cycle is set to be 3.5 million tonnes over the previous cycle.
"In the spring-summer cycle, we harvested 14.6 million tonnes of cron and the autumn-winter cycle will come in around 3.5 million tonnes," he added.

Conasupo, the state-owned staples agency and other corn end users currently have stocks between 2.5 million and three million tonnes, Castellanos said. The farm leader is also chairman of the National Association of Corn Growers.
